text:
sara: Heads up — telemetry from the last 12h shows a weird pattern for clients hitting /v1/generate after we started the v2 rollout. Some are getting 404s, others get served v2-compatible responses. Can we sync on desired behaviour?

mike: Noted. Are those clients explicitly calling /v1, or are they using Accept-Version: 1 header?

sara: Mostly explicit /v1 path. A few have Accept-Version but inconsistent. We see ~2.3k distinct clients, ~8% error spike on 500/404.

olivia: Runtime log snippet:
```
[2026-03-10T09:21:12Z] route=/v1/generate target=runtime-v2 fallback=false response_code=404 client=svc-123
[2026-03-10T09:21:13Z] route=/v1/generate target=runtime-v2 fallback=true response_code=200 client=svc-456
```
Seems routing layer is sometimes falling back to a compatible v2 model but not consistently.

alex: Analytics side: our routing rules are evaluated in two places: edge-router and the longtail router. They have slightly different grammar for version matching. We probably have a policy drift.

jasmine: Product question — what's the UX we want? Ideally we deter clients from relying on implicit fallbacks long-term. For now we should aim for predictable behavior and good telemetry so integrators can fix.

mike: Proposal A: strict deprecation — /v1 routes return 410 after grace window; no implicit fallback. Clients must migrate to /v2 or use version header. Pros: simple, forces migration. Cons: abrupt for some integrators.

mike: Proposal B: soft compatibility — continue serving v1 semantics by routing to v2 models with a compatibility shim for 90 days. Log + increment telemetry tag "compat:shim". Pros: smoother migration. Cons: maintenance cost and masking regressions.

olivia: Technical constraints: our kv-cache and batching logic differ in v2 (kv layout change). Compatibility shim adds ~3-6ms overhead and ~5% higher memory. Also makes canarying harder.

sara: Observability ask: if we choose B we need per-client and per-route flags: migrated=true/false, shim_used=true/false. Console needs a deprecation panel listing top clients by volume, failure rate, and shim usage.

alex: We already emit attrs: version_requested, route, runtime_target, shim_used boolean. But not all dashboards surface shim_used. I can add a per-route chart and a user table if we decide.

jasmine: For UX, can we auto-populate a deprecation notice in the console for teams with high v1 traffic and include a migration guide link + one-click request for extended grace?

sara: One more ops edge: if we route /v1 to v2 with shim=true, tracing spans need to include original_url=/v1/generate so support can correlate traces with customer logs. Right now trace shows /v2/generate which confuses customers.

mike: Ok action list draft:
- Decide policy: strict vs soft (team vote by EOD)
- If soft: add shim_used flag everywhere + increase telemetry retention for 60d
- Add console deprecation panel prototype (product + alex)
- Fix routing grammar mismatch between edge and longtail (eng-platform)
- Update runbooks for canary/fallback testing (eng-oncall + eng-sre)
- Communication plan for customers (commms + account teams)

olivia: Also suggest a third hybrid: hard 410 for unknown clients, soft shim for known customers on allowlist for 30d. That reduces blast radius.

alex: Good idea. We can maintain an allowlist keyed by client_id with TTL. Edge checks allowlist before applying strict 410.

jasmine: If we do allowlist route, product needs an API/UI to add/remove clients and log the reason (support request id).

mike: Vote tally so far: soft=3 (sara, alex, jasmine), strict=1 (mike), hybrid=1 (olivia).

sara: Let's converge on hybrid with 30d allowlist for high-volume customers, shim telemetry enabled globally. I'll open a PR for the deprecation timeline and communication draft.

mike: Sounds good. I'll block a maintenance window for the grammar fix and coordinate with eng-oncall.

olivia: I'll add shim_used to telemetry and push a dashboard patch.

alex: I'll prototype the deprecation panel and allowlist UI in the console.

jasmine: I'll draft the migration messaging and one-click grace request UX.

sara: Thanks everyone — please update the PR with notes and link to the dashboard mock when ready.
